mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a softening labor market (UNRATE < 6%) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when UNRATE jumps > 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate revenues, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% m/m for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during three-month INDPRO declines > -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) over the past two months signals a shift from saving to investment, which boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 2% m/m AND RSAFS rises > 1% m/m over last 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% y/y) signals accommodative monetary policy that supports risk assets, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL growth < 2% y/y
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during prolonged low-rate/low-inflation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons signals labor market softness despite low unemployment, which foreshadows weaker consumer spending and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth < 50,000 in a month when UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during such decoupling events.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 1% combined with a flat industrial production index (INDPRO) over the past quarter signals broad-based demand weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > -1% y/y AND INDPRO change ≈ 0% q/q
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered demand shock episodes.
